source_candidate.name: correlation-admissible multi-instrument evidence sharing with objective-separated acquisition

primary_sources.citation: Chih-Yu Lee et al., Real-time Multi-instrument Autonomous Discovery of Novel Phase-change Memory Materials, arXiv:2605.18033v1, 2026-05-18
On Negative Transfer and Structure of Latent Functions in Multi-output Gaussian Processes, arXiv:2004.02382

verified: The MAD paper uses distinct acquisition objectives: XRD structural mapping uses maximum uncertainty over phase abundances, while resistance optimization uses expected improvement.
The physical instrument latencies are strongly asymmetric in the paper: one XRD measurement is about 15 minutes and one electrical measurement about 1.5 minutes.

The model shares information through a rank-one coregionalized multi-output GP over seven NMF structural outputs plus resistance, and the in-silico study explicitly compares coregionalized versus independent kernels and Bayesian optimization versus random sampling over 10 random seeds.

The in-silico results support the direction that coregionalized BO reconstructs the XRD map with fewer samples/lower DTW and approaches the resistance optimum faster than the compared independent/random variants in this material-system simulation.

The arXiv abstract reports 25 closed-loop iterations and a seven-fold speed-up; the body separately reports a single live run completing the simultaneous tasks within about five hours and elsewhere describes at-least/about five-fold acceleration under other comparison wordings.

Generic multi-output-GP primary literature independently supports the boundary condition that forcing unrelated outputs to share structure can cause negative transfer relative to independent/subset models.

material_scope_corrections.claim: Schedule heterogeneous instruments using their actual measurement costs/latencies.
material_scope_corrections.correction: The paper says the current architecture distributes time/data points uniformly across tasks and the faster electrical process idles while waiting for XRD; the diffractometer is the throughput bottleneck. An asynchronous multi-agent architecture that avoids this idling is described as future work, not as the tested controller.

material_scope_corrections.claim: 25 iterations in about five hours with roughly seven-fold speed-up.
material_scope_corrections.correction: The 25-iteration/seven-fold pair is an abstract headline; the about-five-hour statement describes a single live run; at-least/about-five-fold statements elsewhere use different comparison language. These are not one matched wall-clock causal estimate and must not be fused into a single denominator-free speed claim.

material_scope_corrections.claim: A dynamic correlation-admissibility gate suppresses sharing when support is weak.
material_scope_corrections.correction: MAD uses fixed coregionalization in the reported system. The paper notes that correlation benefits are not universal, and separate multi-output-GP theory establishes negative-transfer risk, but no online admit/revoke gate is implemented or evaluated in the cited MAD experiments.

material_scope_corrections.claim: The 95% structural-similarity result is an isolated threshold comparison against independent GPs.
material_scope_corrections.correction: The paper reports reaching about 95% structural similarity around 42 XRD measurements and Figure 4 shows the coregionalized strategy leading the compared curves; the text does not provide a standalone formal sample-count-at-95%-threshold test for every comparator.

tested_scope: arXiv:2605.18033v1 physical Mn-Sb-Te MAD loop and its reported in-silico benchmark, plus generic negative-transfer theory from arXiv:2004.02382; no claim about production prevalence, arbitrary instrument sets, or a tested dynamic correlation-admission controller
downstream_note: Use this as evidence for objective-separated acquisition plus correlation-based posterior sharing under demonstrated output correlation. Do not use it as evidence that the tested MAD controller already performs latency/cost-aware scheduling or dynamic correlation revocation.
